root_cause.text: In sve_set_common(), the code to set TIF_SVE (and clear SVCR_SM_MASK) for SVE writes was incorrectly placed inside a conditional block guarded by `system_supports_sme()`, so on systems with SVE but without SME, TIF_SVE was not set, leaving the task in an inconsistent state with SVE register data in FP_STATE_SVE format but TIF_SVE clear.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves the switch statement (which sets TIF_SVE for ARM64_VEC_SVE and TIF_SME for ARM64_VEC_SME) outside the `if (system_supports_sme())` block, as described in the commit message: "This bug was introduced during rework ... where the setting of TIF_SVE was moved into a block which is only executed when system_supports_sme() is true." The diff shows the removal of the `if (system_supports_sme()) { ... }` wrapper.

The diff shows the removal of the `if (system_supports_sme()) { ... }` wrapper.

candidates.rationale: This condition gates the entire block that sets TIF_SVE and clears SVCR_SM_MASK for SVE writes, so on systems without SME, these critical operations are skipped, leaving TIF_SVE unset and state inconsistent.
This line clears SVCR_SM_MASK for SVE writes, but it is only executed when system_supports_sme() is true, so it is not performed on systems with SVE only, contributing to the inconsistent state.
This line sets TIF_SVE for SVE writes, but it is inside the system_supports_sme() guard, so it is not set on systems without SME, directly causing the vulnerability described in the root cause.
This line sets SVCR_SM_MASK for SME writes; while correct for SME, its presence inside the same guard highlights that the SVE-specific operations are incorrectly placed under the SME condition.
This line sets TIF_SME for SME writes; it is part of the same conditional block that incorrectly contains the SVE operations, illustrating the structural flaw.

This WARN_ON_ONCE is inside the default case of the switch, which is itself inside the system_supports_sme() guard. Its placement is part of the overall incorrect structure that isolates SVE-related logic behind the SME check.
This return statement in the default case is also inside the guard, contributing to the flawed control flow where SVE handling is only reachable when SME is supported.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement sets TIF_SVE for SVE writes, but it is placed inside the system_supports_sme() guard. On systems with SVE but without SME, it is never executed, leaving TIF_SVE clear despite the register state being in FP_STATE_SVE format, directly causing the inconsistent state described in the root cause.

This statement clears SVCR_SM_MASK for SVE writes, but it is only executed when system_supports_sme() is true. On SVE-only systems, it is skipped, and the SVCR state may remain inconsistent with the expected SVE-only usage, contributing to the vulnerability.

This conditional guard incorrectly encloses the SVE-specific operations (setting TIF_SVE and clearing SVCR_SM_MASK). By making their execution dependent on SME support, it ensures that on systems without SME these critical operations are omitted, leading to the inconsistent state.

This statement sets SVCR_SM_MASK for SME writes. While appropriate for SME, its presence inside the same system_supports_sme() guard highlights the structural flaw that SVE operations are also placed there. It is part of the problematic control flow that results in SVE writes being mishandled on !SME systems.

This statement sets TIF_SME for SME writes. Similar to the other operations inside the guard, it contributes to the overall flawed structure where SVE-specific code is incorrectly conditioned on SME support, though the direct vulnerability is the missing TIF_SVE set.

This WARN_ON_ONCE is inside the default case of a switch that is itself inside the system_supports_sme() guard. Its placement is a consequence of the flawed control flow structure that isolates SVE handling behind the SME check. While not directly causing the state inconsistency, it is part of the same erroneous block.

This return statement is inside the default case of the switch within the system_supports_sme() guard. It participates in the same incorrect control flow that prevents proper handling of SVE writes on systems without SME. Including it helps illustrate the full extent of the vulnerable code region.
